Recall that a prorepresentable functor is a deformation functor, see
Example <REF_0001>. Thus
if <MATH_0001> is equivalent to a smooth prorepresentable groupoid in
functors, then conditions (1), (2), and (3) follow from
Lemma <REF_0002> (1), (2), and (3).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Conversely, assume conditions (1), (2), and (3) hold. Condition (1)
implies that (S1) and (S2) are satisfied, see
Lemma <REF_0003>.
By
Lemma <REF_0004>
there exists a versal formal object <MATH_0002>. Setting
<MATH_0003> the
associated map <MATH_0004> is smooth (this is
the definition of a versal formal object).
Let <MATH_0005> be the groupoid in functors constructed in
Lemma <REF_0005>
from the map <MATH_0006>. By
Lemma <REF_0006>
we see that <MATH_0007> is a smooth groupoid in functors and that
<MATH_0008> is an equivalence. By
Lemma <REF_0007>
we see that <MATH_0009> is prorepresentable.
Hence <MATH_0010> is the desired presentation of <MATH_0011>.
